headline.purpose: Page headings and the brand word.

fact.purpose: Lifetime and budget beside a decision. Phone decision buttons.

body.purpose: Body text, table cells, item names at 600 or 700, nav links at 500.

label.purpose: Meta lines, captions, help text and key hints.

mono.purpose: Account IDs and request versions only.

stamp-date.purpose: Due dates in tables, slips and lists.

stamp-date-large.purpose: The one due date at the top of an account page or loan card.

stamp-word.purpose: APPROVED, DENIED, WITHDRAWN, EXPIRED, FAILED, CLOSED, OVERDUE, and the role badge.

scrim.purpose: Behind the dialog. The only raised surface.

motion.name: stamp-land
motion.value: 90ms steps(2, jump-none); from scale(1.12) rotate(0deg) to scale(1) at the stamp's own turn (-1.8, 1.3 or -1 deg)
motion.purpose: Approve and +7d. Two frames, no fade. Skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: live-dot-blink
motion.purpose: The live-update dot, once for each update. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

stampBlend.purpose: The blend mode of every stamp, so card stock shows through the ink.

narrative.overview:
Every playground account is a loan from the playplace desk. It is stamped
out, due back, renewed and returned. The interface is the date-due card from
a library book: a shelf-green shell, card-stock desk surfaces, and violet
date stamps that a person can read from across the room. A due date and a
decision are stamped facts, not muted metadata.

The system is dense and calm, because people use it daily across more than
100 accounts. Most of the page is paper and ground with one-pixel rules.
Card stock appears only where a person decides or reads a due date. The one
expressive move is the stamp: a turned, inked mark that lands in two frames.
Everything else is square, flat and quiet.

The design rejects two things that the maintainer named: the generic grey cloud
dashboard with summary tiles over a plain table, and the toy-like look of
the old ball-pit colors. The tool controls real AWS spend.
keyCharacteristics: A shelf-green shell, paper panels on a warm grey ground, and card stock for the desk and the date-due column.
Violet Courier Prime stamps for every due date, turned 1 to 2 degrees.
One sans-serif face at five fixed sizes, with tabular figures.
Flat surfaces with 1 px rules. No shadows anywhere.
One motion: the stamp lands in two frames over 90 ms.
Status is always a word and an icon, never color alone.

rules.name: The Shelf Owns the Shell Rule
rules.body: Shelf green fills the shell and nothing else. In the content area, green appears only as shelf ink: a healthy icon, the meter fill, the CLOSED stamp and the live dot. No content button is green.

rules.name: The Card Stock Is the Desk Rule
rules.body: Card stock marks the places where someone decides or reads a due date: the approval desk, the date-due column and the loan card. A plain list or a form sits on paper.

rules.name: The Red Ink Rule
rules.body: Red text is always red ink (#A8262F). Overdue red (#C8323C) is only for icons and bars, because red on card stock is 4.1:1 and fails for text.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Text uses 19 or 17, 16, 14, 13.5 and 12 pixels, and nothing between. A mockup value of 11, 11.5, 12.5, 13, 15, 18, 20 or 26 pixels snaps to the step whose job it does. The phone uses the same steps.

rules.name: The Stamp Face Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime sets stamped dates, account IDs and request versions, and nothing else. Monospace is never a "technical" costume for labels, numbers or headings.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: The page root sets tabular lining figures, so every number lines up in columns, in every type role. Letter spacing never goes below -0.03em.

rules.name: The Desktop Fleet Rule
rules.body: The full fleet table is a desktop surface and scrolls sideways before it collapses. A phone shows one request or one account, never the fleet.

rules.name: The Flat Desk Rule
rules.body: No `box-shadow` on any surface. If something needs to stand out, it gets a rule, card stock or a stamp.

rules.name: The Turned Stamp Rule
rules.body: Only stamps rotate. A stamp turns between 1 and 2 degrees (-1.8, 1.3 or -1 degrees, varied from row to row). Nothing else on the page is rotated.

rules.name: The Word and Icon Rule
rules.body: Every status, health state and outcome shows a word. Color and icon only support the word.

rules.name: The No Toast Rule
rules.body: Feedback appears beside the thing it is about and in the one live region. Nothing floats in from a corner.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The stamp is the only animation, and the live dot is the only other thing that changes on its own. State changes step in two frames and never fade.

dos: Do put card stock (#EDE3CC) only under the approval desk, the date-due column and the loan card.
Do show lifetime and budget as exact 16 px bold facts beside Approve, for example "36 hours" and "$12.50", with the request version.
Do keep the old due date, struck through, above a renewed stamp.
Do use red ink (#A8262F) for every red word, and overdue red (#C8323C) only for icons and bars.
Do theme the browser surfaces: a violet selection with paper text, a violet caret and `accent-color`, and a 2 px violet focus ring that turns card stock on the shell.
Do keep every text pair at 4.5:1 or more, and the border of every field, select, checkbox and segmented control at 3:1 or more, in both palettes. A button is identified by its label.
Do name the row in every row action for screen readers, for example "Approve priya-glue-etl".
Do make every touch target on the phone at least 44 px.
Do show "unavailable" or "unknown" when a value failed to load.
donts: Don't add a shadow to any surface.
Don't fade anything, or animate anything except the stamp and the live dot.
Don't set anything in Courier Prime except stamped dates, account IDs and request versions.
Don't add a font size between the five steps.
Don't build summary tiles over a plain table, or any generic grey admin dashboard.
Don't bring back the ball-pit colors. The tool must not look toy-like.
Don't use a toast, or a modal for a task that needs no interruption.
Don't signal a status with color alone.
Don't round a deciding fact to "1 day" or "$12".
Don't put a colored stripe wider than 1 px on the side of a card, row or note, or a small label above a heading.
Don't ship inline `style` attributes or a font from a third-party host. The CSP allows neither.
